classification.difficultyReason: Divide a relation into restricted functions and justify that each restriction has an inverse.

content.prompt: Consider the graph of the circle $x^2+y^2=49$. Show that it is possible, in a natural way, to divide the circle into four pieces, each of which is the graph of a function that has an inverse.

answer.worked:
The coordinate axes divide the circle into four quadrant arcs. Solving for $y$ gives the upper and lower semicircles:

$\begin{aligned}y^2&=49-x^2\\y&=\pm\sqrt{49-x^2}.\end{aligned}$

Restrict each semicircle to the left and right halves:

$\begin{aligned}f_1(x)&=\sqrt{49-x^2},&&-7\le x\le0,\\f_2(x)&=\sqrt{49-x^2},&&0\le x\le7,\\f_3(x)&=-\sqrt{49-x^2},&&-7\le x\le0,\\f_4(x)&=-\sqrt{49-x^2},&&0\le x\le7.\end{aligned}$

Every vertical line meets each individual arc at most once, so each arc is the graph of a function. Every horizontal line also meets each individual arc at most once, so each function is one-to-one and has an inverse. Together the four arcs cover the circle, meeting at their endpoints.
